summary: P5's relay Deployment, Service and gate meet the phase's outcome: the environment matches the image's contract in source, both legs resolve against Services this render publishes (server:80, applicationset-controller:7000) with nothing in the rendered NetworkPolicies blocking them, the pinned tag 2485 exists in the registry, the exposure annotations match nginx-configurator's real semantics, and two mutations I ran prove the new check_relay assertions bite. Three advisory findings, none blocking: the internet-facing pod runs as root with the default ServiceAccount token against the consult's stated blast radius, the render's one-public-Service invariant is keyed only to the spelling "yes" while the configurator also honours "true", and the comment justifying the :80 leg names a TLS-handshake failure that cannot occur with server.insecure set.

findings.summary: The relay pod runs as root with the default ServiceAccount token automounted and no securityContext, so a compromise yields more than the HMAC secret the consult's §2 blast radius claims.

check_relay's "only the relay is internet-facing" assertion matches the literal "yes" while nginx-configurator's parse_bool also treats "true" as public, so a second public Service could pass the gate.
The comment justifying the :80 leg says a 443 leg fails on the TLS handshake, but server.insecure makes 443 target the same plain-HTTP port 8080, so it would succeed.
